# Suffocation Medications
Suffocation damage is asphyxiation and blood loss: not breathing, damaged lungs, a stopped heart or bleeding out. Fix the cause first, whether that's the airway, the lungs, the heart or the bleeding, or the damage keeps coming back.
- [bold]Dexalin[/bold]: the standard suffocation medicine. It also clears respiratory strain. Overdose at 30 units. - [bold]Dexalin Plus[/bold]: works faster than dexalin, but overdoses at only 5 units. Measure it carefully. - [bold]Albuterol[/bold]: heals suffocation damage and clears respiratory strain. Overdose at 20 units. - [bold]Inaprovaline[/bold]: a stabilizer. If the lungs still work, it lets a patient keep breathing even in cardiac arrest, and it heals suffocation damage while they're critical. It's also a weak painkiller. Its overdose is very high, at 110 units, but an overdose damages the heart. - [bold]Tricordrazine[/bold]: heals a little of everything, suffocation included.
Breathing from an [bold]oxygen tank[/bold] on internals clears suffocation damage three times as fast. The medical supply vendor stocks medical oxygen tanks and medical gas masks for this.
Blood loss won't go away with medicine. Stop the bleeding and replace the blood with blood packs or an IV drip.
